reasoning_content:
Exit code 141 is SIGPIPE (probably due to `which unzip tar` not finding something in a pipeline with ldd, or due to pipe handling). In any case, x86_64, glibc 2.35. Next I'll install Node.js and Bun. I'll use curl to install Bun from the official installer (bun's install script) — this is the official package. And I'll install Node.js via NodeSource or the apt version.

Ubuntu 22.04's apt nodejs is v12, which is too old. Better options: NodeSource's setup script, or downloading Node.js binaries from nodejs.org. Downloading the official Node.js binary tarball is straightforward and non-interactive.

Plan:
1. Download the Node.js 20 LTS (or 18+) linux-x64 tarball from nodejs.org and install it to /usr/local.
2. Install bun via the official installer: `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash` — this is a pipe-to-shell operation. Per the security rules, pipe-to-shell commands are flagged as HIGH risk. However, this is the standard way to install bun. Alternatively, I could download the bun release binary directly from GitHub. The GitHub releases for oven-sh/bun are at https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases — I can grab the latest release and download bun-linux-x64.zip. This is cleaner: download the binary, unzip it, and move it to /usr/local/bin.

First, let me check for the presence of unzip.
